source_user: Calculation case 44: a model has 48 layers, 8 KV heads, head dimension 96, sequence length 1536, and BF16/FP16 KV values. Estimate bytes for one request's K/V cache. Show the formula and report GiB.
source_assistant: Use 2 × layers × sequence_length × KV_heads × head_dim × bytes_per_value. Here this is 2 × 48 × 1536 × 8 × 96 × 2 = 226492416 bytes = 0.210938 GiB. This excludes allocator metadata and other runtime memory.
corrected_answer:
Mechanism first. A decoder caches one K vector and one V vector per layer per generated/prefilled token, per KV head. With grouped-query attention the cache is sized by num_key_value_heads (here 8), not by the number of query heads, because query heads inside a group share the same K/V. So the exact byte count for a single request is

  bytes = 2 (K and V) x layers x seq_len x kv_heads x head_dim x bytes_per_value
        = 2 x 48 x 1536 x 8 x 96 x 2
        = 226,492,416 bytes = 216.000 MiB = 0.210938 GiB

(GiB here means bytes / 2^30; if a dashboard reports GB = 10^9 the same cache reads as 0.226492 GB, which is a common source of apparent disagreement.) BF16 and FP16 are both 2 bytes/value, so the dtype choice does not change this number; it only changes numerical range behaviour in the attention accumulation.

Boundary conditions under which this formula is the right one: exactly one request at the full 1536-token context; dense causal attention in every layer (no sliding-window, no local/global interleave, no cross-attention or Mamba/linear-attention layers); no MLA-style latent compression, which stores a single low-rank latent per token instead of per-head K and V and breaks this formula entirely; head_dim uniform across layers; and no cross-request prefix sharing.

What the formula deliberately excludes, and which is what actually decides how many concurrent requests fit:
1. Paged KV block granularity. Engines allocate in blocks (commonly 16 or 32 tokens), so real usage is ceil(1536/block_size) x block_size tokens, and the last partial block is wasted. At block_size=16 this case is exact (1536 is divisible by 16), but any sequence length that is not a multiple of the block size rounds up.
2. Allocator fragmentation and the engine's pre-reserved KV pool, which is normally sized once at startup from gpu_memory_utilization minus weights and activation workspace.
3. Tensor parallelism. KV heads are sharded across TP ranks only when kv_heads is divisible by the TP degree. With kv_heads=8, TP degrees that do not divide 8 force KV-head replication, so per-GPU KV memory is larger than total/TP. Check this before assuming linear scaling.
4. Speculative decoding, beam search, and n>1 sampling multiply the live KV footprint by the number of concurrent branches unless the engine forks pages copy-on-write.

Falsifiable prediction and how to test it: if you run a single request at exactly this context length on an idle GPU, the steady-state KV allocation attributable to that request should be within a few percent of 216.000 MiB. Serve with the KV pool sized so it is the only variable, drive one request, and diff torch.cuda.memory_reserved() (or the engine's reported free KV blocks x bytes-per-block) before and after prefill. If the measured delta exceeds the prediction by more than ~10%, the assumptions above are violated somewhere: verify kv_heads vs query heads, block rounding, KV dtype actually in use, and TP replication.

Evidence to collect before using this number for capacity planning: the served model's config.json (num_hidden_layers, num_key_value_heads, head_dim or hidden_size/num_attention_heads), the engine startup log line reporting KV cache dtype, block size and total GPU KV blocks, the TP/PP topology, and a measured concurrency ramp.

Rollback gate: derive max concurrency as usable_KV_pool_bytes / per_request_bytes, then deploy at no more than 70-80% of that to absorb block rounding, fragmentation and length variance. If p99 latency degrades, preemption/recompute counters rise above a low single-digit percentage of requests, or any OOM appears, roll back to the previous max-concurrency setting immediately rather than trimming the KV pool further.
risks: Bare formula omits paged-KV block rounding, the pre-reserved KV pool and allocator fragmentation, so sizing concurrency directly from it overcommits the GPU and invites OOM or request preemption.
The count uses KV heads; applying the same number to an MHA checkpoint (or confusing num_attention_heads with num_key_value_heads) understates KV memory by the GQA group factor.
With kv_heads=8, tensor-parallel degrees that do not divide 8 replicate KV heads across ranks, so per-GPU footprint exceeds total/TP and naive linear scaling is wrong.
